findings.reason: the section's whole seam is this composer, and the sentence leaves an implementing node unable to tell whether to keep the XOR or pass both, so the plan-naming branch would silently regress to the exact defect the prior review raised.
findings.text: §9 states "`_review_dispatch_tokens` now chooses `--brief` or `--plan`/`--section`, never both; for a run that names a plan it passes both", two incompatible behaviours for one composer in one clause; the code emits the pair as an either/or (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:597-601`) and `_review_dispatch_fields` blanks the brief whenever a plan is set (`brief = "" if plan else …`, line 503), so "passes both" is not reachable by changing `_review_dispatch_tokens` alone, and a node that follows the "never both" half emits `--brief` alone for a plan-naming run, dropping `--plan`/`--section` and breaking the invariant the same sentence cites at lines 496-502

findings.reason: an implementation that emits `--brief` alone for a plan-naming run satisfies "the first brief contains the SCORE block" and passes the gate while dropping the plan authority the section must keep.
findings.text: §9's done-when composes the reflex review of an implement run, an investigate run and a brief-carried run, and asserts the brief text and the brief-carried path, but it never asserts that a plan-naming run's composed command still carries `--plan`/`--section`, so the plan-authority half of the section's own mechanism is measured by nothing
